reason: This passage (Exodus 3-4, the call of Moses at the burning bush) depicts God expressing compassion for the Israelites suffering in Egypt and commissioning Moses to lead them to freedom. The text emphasizes God 'seeing' the people's affliction (רָאֹה רָאִיתִי אֶת־ עֳנִי עַמִּי), 'hearing' their cry, and 'knowing' their sorrows. The only anger mentioned (וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה) is directed at Moses personally for his reluctance to accept his mission, not at the people for improper worship. The passage concludes with the people believing and worshiping God after hearing of His visitation (וַֽיִּשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ). The text contains no evidence of the people worshiping improperly or of God being angered at them for such behavior.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
